commit.message:
[Core/Auth] Reject auth headers on HTTP servers with auth disabled, and refuse disabled mode with K8s token auth (#67150)

## Description

A dashboard started with `RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled` accepts every request,
so a jobs, state or Serve client in token mode works against it and
never tells the user that the two sides disagree. This PR makes Ray's
HTTP servers (dashboard head, dashboard agent, runtime env agent) in
disabled mode reject any request that carries an `Authorization` header,
of any scheme, or a non-empty `X-Ray-Authorization`, with 401 and the
same error a client without a token gets, the rule #67052 added for
gRPC.

It also makes `RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled` with `ENABLE_K8S_TOKEN_AUTH` a
config error and removes that combination's exemptions. Today that
combination can't start: the head's GCS rejects its own client with
`InvalidAuthToken`.

```diff
 token_auth_middleware  (dashboard head, dashboard agent, runtime env agent)
   auth disabled
+    any Authorization header or X-Ray-Authorization -> 401 + token auth error
     otherwise -> pass
   auth on
     missing token -> 401, wrong token -> 403

 disabled mode, decided by RAY_AUTH_MODE
-  C++ gRPC server: server token empty and not ENABLE_K8S_TOKEN_AUTH
-  syncer: server token empty and not ENABLE_K8S_TOKEN_AUTH
-  Python gRPC interceptor, HTTP middleware: exempt under ENABLE_K8S_TOKEN_AUTH
+  all of them: RAY_AUTH_MODE != token, no exemption

 RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled + ENABLE_K8S_TOKEN_AUTH
+  Node.__init__ (ray start, ray.init(), Cluster()), flag from env or system config
+    -> ValueError before starting anything
+  AuthenticationTokenLoader::GetToken (GCS, raylet, drivers) -> fatal with the same message
```

- The no-token error and the AuthModeMismatch error are now one message,
`TOKEN_AUTH_ERROR_MESSAGE` (Python) and `kTokenAuthErrorMessage`
(`src/ray/common/constants.h`): "Token authentication is enabled on this
client, but it has no token or the cluster has token authentication
disabled." followed by `TOKEN_AUTH_FIX_MESSAGE`, which names both fixes.
The token loader raises it for a missing token, and the gRPC servers,
the syncer and the HTTP middleware return it in disabled mode.
- The `ray-authentication-token` cookie doesn't count, so a browser that
kept a cookie from an earlier token-mode cluster at the same address
isn't locked out. Over HTTP, an empty `Authorization` or
`X-Ray-Authorization` header doesn't count either; gRPC still rejects an
`authorization` key with an empty value.
- Paths that need no token, such as `/api/version`, `/api/healthz` and
`/api/authentication_mode`, still need none, but a request that sends an
auth header is rejected.
- Ray's own processes send no token in a disabled cluster: the raylet
and the dashboard head attach one only in token mode, so the agents see
the rule only from token-mode clients or outside callers.
- With one message for both cases, the special cases go away:
`AuthenticationError.__str__` no longer checks for the mismatch text,
and `format_authentication_http_error` returns that message for any 401
instead of `Authentication required: {body}` plus the no-token text,
which would print it twice. The jobs, state and Serve SDKs raise it as
`AuthenticationError` through the existing 401 handling.
- The C++ gRPC server and the syncer used to treat an empty server token
as disabled mode. Kubernetes token auth runs in token mode with an empty
server token, so they now read `RAY_AUTH_MODE` instead. A unit test
checks that such a server rejects a bad token with `InvalidAuthToken`,
not the token auth error; a valid Kubernetes token being accepted needs
a real TokenReview, which the KubeRay check in #67057 covers.
- The config error reads `Kubernetes token authentication
(ENABLE_K8S_TOKEN_AUTH) requires RAY_AUTH_MODE=token. Set
RAY_AUTH_MODE=token, or turn off ENABLE_K8S_TOKEN_AUTH to run with auth
disabled.` The C++ side logs it with `RAY_LOG(FATAL)` rather than
`RAY_CHECK`, whose message would call it a bug in Ray.

A client in token mode with a token file, against a head started with
`RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled`:

- **Before:** `JobSubmissionClient(url).list_jobs()` and
`list_nodes(address=url)` return normally.
- **After:** `ray job submit` and `ray list nodes` exit 1 with
`ray.exceptions.AuthenticationError: Token authentication is enabled on
this client, but it has no token or the cluster has token authentication
disabled. To connect to a cluster with token authentication, …` (the
full fix text, once), and `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer x'` gets 401
with the same text. With `RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled` set on the client, the
job succeeds and `ray list nodes` lists the node.

With `RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled RAY_ENABLE_K8S_TOKEN_AUTH=1`:

- **Before:** `ray start --head` exits 1 with `InvalidAuthToken:
Authentication token is missing or incorrect`.
- **After:** `ray start --head` and `ray.init()` exit before starting
any process with the config error, and `gcs_server` started directly
exits 1 with the same message.

## Related issues

Closes #67053

## Additional information

A client in token mode against a server with auth disabled used to work
and now fails. To fix it, set `RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled` on the client
too. A reverse proxy in front of a disabled cluster that adds its own
`Authorization` header, Bearer or Basic, is rejected the same way. The
proxy has to strip the header, or the cluster has to turn on token auth
(#67056 documents this). The change touches no stored state, so it is
easy to revert.

---------

Signed-off-by: Chi-Sheng Liu <chishengliu@chishengliu.com>

commit.message:
[Fix][Core/Auth] Enable token auth in C++ and Java drivers that start their own local cluster (#66778)

## Description

Since #64755, `ray start --head` enables token auth when `RAY_AUTH_MODE`
is unset and `~/.ray/auth_token` exists, for example after any earlier
Python `ray.init()`. C++ and Java drivers that start their own head
don't make the same decision: their auth mode stays `disabled`, so they
connect without a token and fail with `InvalidAuthToken`. The release
sanity check hits this. #66467 fixed the same mismatch for Python
`ray.init()`.

This PR adds `MaybeEnableTokenAuthIfTokenAvailable()` next to the token
loader. When `RAY_AUTH_MODE` is unset and a token exists, it sets
`RAY_AUTH_MODE=token` in the process environment so that the later
`RayConfig` re-initialization keeps it. Both drivers call it, only when
they started the head:

```diff
 ProcessHelper::RayStart (C++)
   if driver && no address
+    MaybeEnableTokenAuthIfTokenAvailable()
     StartRayNode()  # ray start --head

 RayNativeRuntime.start (Java)
   if driver && no address
     RunManager.startRayHead()  # ray start --head
   if driver
     loadLibrary()
+    if started the head
+      nativeMaybeEnableTokenAuthIfTokenAvailable()
     getGcsClient()
```

Drivers given an explicit address are unchanged. `//cpp:metric_example`
now runs without `RAY_AUTH_MODE` to cover this path.

## Related issues

N/A

## Additional information

N/A

commit.message:
[Feat][Core/Auth] Enable token authentication for local clusters by default (#64755)

## Description

Enable token authentication for local clusters by default.

The table below shows the resulting behavior. Remote and worker paths
are unchanged.

| Entry point | `RAY_AUTH_MODE` unset, token exists | `RAY_AUTH_MODE`
unset, no token | `RAY_AUTH_MODE=token` | `RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`ray.init()`** (new local cluster, no address) | enable + **reuse**
token + **warn** | enable + **generate** token + **warn** | enable
(generate/reuse), no warning | disabled, no warning |
| **`ray start --head`** (local head) | enable + reuse token + **warn**
| disabled + **warn** | enable; **raises** if no token, no warning |
disabled, no warning |
| **`ray.init(address=…)`** (connect to existing) | unchanged, no
auto-enable; needs token if cluster requires it | unchanged | requires
token, else error | disabled |
| **`ray start --address=…`** (worker) | unchanged, no auto-enable |
unchanged | requires token, else error | disabled |

A token "exists" if any of these resolve, checked in order:

1. `RAY_AUTH_TOKEN` environment variable
2. file at `RAY_AUTH_TOKEN_PATH`
3. default file `~/.ray/auth_token`

## Related issues
N/A

## Additional information

To enable this for all clusters in the future:

- Change the default to "token" here:
https://github.com/ray-project/ray/blob/1439e47b9b136143fbc99417cb4f50a82eff72a9/src/ray/common/ray_config_def.h#L39.
That is the single source of truth, and `RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled` stays
as the opt-out.
- Remove the auto-enable helper functions from this PR
(`enable_token_auth_by_default`,
`maybe_enable_token_auth_if_token_available`) and their call sites in
`worker.py` and `scripts.py`.
- Decide whether `ray start --head` should auto-generate a token instead
of erroring. The worker and connect paths would then require a
distributed token, which is a breaking change.
- The cluster launcher, KubeRay, and autoscaler would need to distribute
the token to workers automatically. Test fixtures would need to
provision a token, and every client path would need to attach it.
- Update `token-auth.md` and the guides that say "disabled by default".

---------

Signed-off-by: Chi-Sheng Liu <chishengliu@chishengliu.com>

commit.message:
[Core/Auth] Reject gRPC requests that carry a token on clusters with auth disabled (#67147)

## Description

A gRPC server with no auth token accepts every request, so a driver or
node in token mode connects to a cluster started with
`RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled` without any error, and nothing tells the user
that the two sides disagree. With this PR, a server in disabled mode
rejects any request that carries a token with `UNAUTHENTICATED` and
`AuthModeMismatch: cluster has RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled; set it on the
client too`.

```diff
 ServerCall::ValidateAuthenticationToken  (src/ray/rpc/server_call.h)
   if server has no token and K8s token auth is off
-    accept
+    request has no token -> accept
+    request has a token  -> UNAUTHENTICATED "AuthModeMismatch: ..."
   else
     missing or wrong token -> UNAUTHENTICATED "InvalidAuthToken: ..."
```

- The Python gRPC server interceptor
(`grpc_authentication_server_interceptor.py`) applies the same rule, and
`create_grpc_server_with_interceptors` now installs it in every auth
mode. The dashboard agent now builds its gRPC server with that helper
instead of its own token-mode-only copy.
- The RaySyncer stream (`ray_syncer_server.cc`) applies the same rule.
- All of these keep the Kubernetes exception (`ENABLE_K8S_TOKEN_AUTH`).
The message is one constant on each side,
`kAuthModeMismatchErrorMessage` in `src/ray/common/constants.h` and
`AUTH_MODE_MISMATCH_ERROR_MESSAGE` in `authentication_constants.py`.
- `ValidateAuthenticationToken` now returns a `Status` instead of a
bool, so the reply carries the reason for the rejection.
- `AuthenticationError.__str__` returns AuthModeMismatch messages as
they are, without `TOKEN_AUTH_FIX_MESSAGE`, because the fix is to opt
out of auth, not to get a token.

A driver in token mode with a token file, against a head started with
`RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled`:

- **Before:** `ray.init(address=...)` connects and runs tasks without
auth.
- **After:** `ray.init(address=...)` raises at once with
`ray.exceptions.AuthenticationError: RPC error: AuthModeMismatch:
cluster has RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled; set it on the client too`. `ray
start --address` fails the same way. The same driver with
`RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled` still connects, even with the token file
present.

HTTP clients are out of scope; #67053 covers them.

## Related issues

Closes #67052

## Additional information

This changes behavior for anyone who runs a client in token mode against
a cluster that has auth disabled. Those connections used to work and now
fail with AuthModeMismatch. The fix for them is to set
`RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled` on the client too. The change is easy to
revert, since it touches no stored state. Two cases hit this without the
user choosing token mode:

- Until #67055 removes the local-cluster special cases, a bare
`ray.init()` turns on token mode when `~/.ray/auth_token` exists. If the
local head started before that file existed, it runs with auth off, and
that `ray.init()` now fails with AuthModeMismatch. This only affects
master between this PR and #67055, since all of #67047 ships in one
release.
- A `ray://` client that passes its own `authorization` metadata, for
example for a proxy in front of a cluster with auth off, is now
rejected. Such a proxy credential has to move to another metadata key.

The Python interceptor now also runs on servers that skipped it in
disabled mode: the Ray Client server and proxier, the dashboard agent,
and the Serve replica's internal gRPC server. Serve's user-facing gRPC
ingress (`gRPCGenericServer`) doesn't use this interceptor, and the
replica's internal server gets user request metadata inside the request
body, not as gRPC headers, so a user's own `authorization` header never
reaches it.

Test helpers that send the test process's token whatever the cluster's
mode (`kill_raylet`, `RayletKiller` and the `DrainNode` calls in
`test_failure_4.py`) now go through `call_with_auth_token` in
`ray._private.test_utils`, which retries without the token when the
cluster answers AuthModeMismatch.

commit.message:
[Docs][Core/Auth] Document that worker nodes need RAY_AUTH_MODE=token to join a token-auth head (#67096)

## Description

`ray start --head` turns on token authentication when a token is
available, for example when `~/.ray/auth_token` exists. `ray start
--address` doesn't, so a worker started next to that head node fails to
join even on the same machine. Setting `RAY_AUTH_TOKEN` alone doesn't
help either:

| Worker command | Result |
|---|---|
| `ray start --address=<head-node-ip>:6379` | Fails |
| `RAY_AUTH_TOKEN=$(ray get-auth-token) ray start
--address=<head-node-ip>:6379` | Fails |
| `RAY_AUTH_MODE=token ray start --address=<head-node-ip>:6379` | Joins
|

This PR adds a paragraph to the "Local development with ray start"
section of `doc/source/ray-security/token-auth.md`. It says worker nodes
don't enable token authentication automatically and shows the command
that works.

## Related issues

commit.message:
[core] Replace RAY_AUTH_MODE=k8s with separate config to enable Kubernetes token authentication (#59621)

## Description

Per discussion from REP PR
(https://github.com/ray-project/enhancements/pull/63), this PR adds a
server-side config `RAY_ENABLE_K8S_TOKEN_RBAC=true` to enable
Kubernetes-based token authentication. This must be set in addition to
`RAY_AUTH_MODE=token`. The main benefit of this change is that the
server-side authentication flow becomes opaque to clients, and all
clients only need to set `RAY_AUTH_MODE=token` along with their token.

commit.message:
[Fix][Core/Auth] Pass auth token to image_uri containers and reuse it when `ray.init()` finds a local cluster (#66467)

## Description

`test_runtime_env_container` has failed on master since #64755 enabled
token auth by default for local clusters. That change exposed two bugs:

1. **Container workers can't find the token.** The `image_uri` /
`container` plugin forwards `RAY_AUTH_MODE=token` into the podman worker
but doesn't mount the token file, so the worker crashes on startup. Fix:
mount the token file read-only and set `RAY_AUTH_TOKEN_PATH`. The token
isn't passed via `--env`, because the podman command is logged.
2. **`ray.init()` can't connect to a cluster that `ray start --head`
started with token auth.** With `RAY_AUTH_MODE` unset, the driver
connects without a token and gets rejected. Fix: when `ray.init()` finds
a running local cluster (no `address`, or `address="auto"`) and a token
exists, it enables token auth, reuses the token, and warns, just like
`ray start --head`. An explicit `address` or `RAY_ADDRESS` keeps the
current behavior, and nothing else in the #64755 behavior table changes.

## Related issues

Related to #64755.

commit.message:
[Core/Auth] Fail fast with an actionable error when a node or client has no auth token (#67126)

## Description

A node or client in token mode that has no token, or whose token the
cluster rejects, now fails at once with an error that says how to fix
it.

```diff
 ray start --address / ray.init(address=...)
   Node._init_gcs_client
     up to 20 attempts, 1s apart:
       GcsClient(...)
+      except AuthenticationError: raise
       except Exception: sleep, retry

 ray.init("ray://...")
   Worker.__init__
+    ensure_token_if_auth_enabled(create_token_if_missing=False)
     _connect_channel
       ping_server -> get_cluster_info
+        if UNAUTHENTICATED: raise self._reject(e)
       except grpc.RpcError: sleep, retry
   Worker._can_reconnect   # call, get, data and log retry loops
+    UNAUTHENTICATED -> False
+  Worker._reject          # every rejection, on any thread
+    record the AuthenticationError; the call and get retry loops then raise it
```

The fix text lives in `TOKEN_AUTH_FIX_MESSAGE`
(`python/ray/_private/authentication/authentication_constants.py`): run
`ray get-auth-token` on the head and copy the token to
`~/.ray/auth_token` or to a file `RAY_AUTH_TOKEN_PATH` points to, or set
`RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled` if the cluster opted out. The Python and C++
(`kNoTokenErrorMessage`) no-token messages embed it, and
`AuthenticationError.__str__` appends it to any auth error that doesn't
already contain it. It replaces the old appended help text, which told
clients to run `ray get-auth-token --generate`, even though a token made
on a client can't match the cluster's. The C++ message no longer lists
the `RAY_AUTH_TOKEN` environment variable. Token precedence is
unchanged.

Also:

- `AuthenticationError` now subclasses `ConnectionError`, so existing
`except ConnectionError` handlers around `ray.init(address=...)` still
catch rejections. Two handlers reword a `ConnectionError`: one in
`ray.init` ("Failed to connect to Ray cluster") and one in `serve
controller-health` ("Make sure a Ray cluster is running"). Both now let
`AuthenticationError` through, so the fix text survives.
- `get_auth_headers_if_auth_enabled` raises `AuthenticationError`
instead of logging a warning. It already raised in practice, from the
token loader, and its callers (event agent, aggregator publisher) catch
`Exception` and retry as before.

Measured against a token-auth head on one machine, from an empty HOME:

| Node or client | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `ray start --address`, `RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled` | 21s, `RuntimeError:
Failed to connect to GCS` | 1s, `AuthenticationError` naming both fixes
|
| `ray start --address`, different token | 21s, `RuntimeError: Failed to
connect to GCS` | 1s, `AuthenticationError` naming both fixes |
| `ray://`, `RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled` | 31s, `ConnectionError: ray client
connection timeout` | under 1s, `AuthenticationError` naming both fixes
|
| `ray start --address`, `ray.init(address=...)` or `ray://`, no token |
under 1s, message suggests `ray get-auth-token --generate` | under 1s,
message names both fixes |

`test_rejected_connect_fails_fast_naming_fix` sets
`RAY_NUM_REDIS_GET_RETRIES=60` in each subprocess instead of the cap of
2 that the autouse `pre_envs` fixture sets, so code that still retries a
rejection takes about 60s and fails the test's 20s bound.

## Related issues

Closes #67051

Part of #67047.

## Additional information

This is easy to revert, since it changes no data, config or file format.
It does change behavior that users can see. A `ray://` client whose
token is rejected while it reconnects mid-session now raises
`AuthenticationError` immediately from `ray.put`, `ray.get`, pending
futures and `ray.cluster_resources()`, and calls already retrying in
other threads fail with that same error. Before, the client kept
retrying until the reconnect grace period ran out. Calling
`ray.init("ray://...")` a second time still needs
`ray.util.disconnect()` first, as before this PR, but the error now says
"Ray Client is already initialized" instead of "already connected". This
hasn't been checked with rotating Kubernetes service-account tokens;
#67057 covers that. Code that matched on the old `AuthenticationError`
help text sees the new wording. Until #67049 gives `ray start --head`
its own no-token error, `ray start --head` with `RAY_AUTH_MODE=token`
and no token shows the new client-side message, which says to copy the
token from the head. The old help text pointed to `ray get-auth-token
--generate`.

commit.message:
[Fix][Serve] Fix Serve replica ASGIService bypasses token authentication (#65189)

## Description

Every Serve replica starts an internal `ASGIService` gRPC server for
handle-path traffic. It was built with a raw `grpc.aio.server()` and
bound with `add_insecure_port("[::]:0")`, making it the only Python-side
gRPC server in Ray that skipped both of Ray's transport controls:

- **No authentication.** Under `RAY_AUTH_MODE=token` it still accepted
calls with a missing or invalid token, and reached
`pickle.loads(request.pickled_request_metadata)` (the first statement of
the unary and streaming handlers) before any validation.
- **No TLS.** Every other Ray Python gRPC server binds via
`add_port_to_grpc_server`, which uses mTLS under `RAY_USE_TLS=1`. This
port stayed plaintext.

Both sides of the channel now use Ray's shared helpers:

- `replica.py`
- `grpc.aio.server(...)` →
`create_grpc_server_with_interceptors(asynchronous=True, ...)`
  - `add_insecure_port(...)` → `add_port_to_grpc_server(...)`.
- `request_router/replica_wrapper.py`
- `grpc.aio.insecure_channel(...)` → `init_grpc_channel(...,
asynchronous=True)`.

They must change together: attaching the interceptor while the client
used a raw insecure channel would reject *all* legitimate
inter-deployment traffic under token mode. The user-facing gRPC proxy
ingress and direct-ingress servers are deliberately untouched because
those are the application's public API.

## Related issues
N/A

commit.message:
[Core/Auth] Require the auth token on Ray's Prometheus metrics endpoints (#67128)

## Description

With token auth on, Ray's Prometheus metrics endpoints served metrics to
anyone who could reach them: job, actor and deployment names, node IPs
and resource use. This PR puts the dashboard's token check on Ray's own
metrics endpoints (each node's metrics port, the dashboard head and the
autoscaler) and makes Ray's own Prometheus send the token. The HAProxy
exporter that Serve's HAProxy ingress serves on its own port is not
covered; that's #67211.

```text
metrics request
  auth off                         -> serve metrics (unchanged)
  no token in Authorization,
    X-Ray-Authorization or the
    ray-authentication-token cookie -> 401, WWW-Authenticate: Bearer
  wrong token                      -> 403
  right token                      -> serve metrics
```

The node exporter wraps its WSGI app with the new
`get_token_auth_wsgi_app`. The dashboard head and both autoscaler
monitors switch from `prometheus_client.start_http_server` to
`start_metrics_http_server`, which serves the same registry with the
same address-family choice plus the token check.

With auth on, `ray metrics launch-prometheus` adds an `authorization`
block to the `ray` scrape job in the config it writes,
`./prometheus-<version>.linux-amd64/ray_prometheus.yml`:

```yaml
- job_name: 'ray'
  file_sd_configs:
  - files:
    - '/tmp/ray/prom_metrics_service_discovery.json'
  authorization:
    type: Bearer
    credentials: '<RAY_AUTH_TOKEN>'  # when RAY_AUTH_TOKEN is set
    # otherwise: credentials_file: '<RAY_AUTH_TOKEN_PATH, else ~/.ray/auth_token>'
```

Ray creates that config fresh with mode 0600
(`O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`, after deleting any old file at that path).
`RAY_AUTH_TOKEN` takes precedence over the token file, so when it is
set, the config holds the token inline. Otherwise the block points at
the token file, and `launch-prometheus` exits before downloading
anything if that file is missing, unreadable, empty, or holds more than
one non-blank line, since Prometheus sends the whole file. Ray's C++
token loader (`AuthenticationTokenLoader::ReadTokenFromFile`) now reads
the first non-blank line of a token file instead of the first line, so
blank lines around the token work everywhere. If writing the config
fails, `launch-prometheus` logs the error and exits 1 instead of
printing a traceback. When `RAY_AUTH_MODE` is unset and
`launch-prometheus` finds no token, it warns that every Ray target
returns 401 if the cluster runs token auth. With auth off, the config is
unchanged. The dashboard's `prometheus.yml` in the session folder is a
template for users who run their own Prometheus. It gets no
`authorization` block, so those users add it themselves.

`launch-prometheus` decides whether auth is on the way `ray start` does
(`maybe_enable_token_auth_if_token_available`), so local clusters that
have token auth on by default are scraped with the token.

Tests that scrape metrics endpoints directly now send the token:
`fetch_raw_prometheus`, the Serve metrics tests and conftest,
`test_tls_auth.py`, and the vLLM batch release test.
`fetch_raw_prometheus` also raises `HTTPError` on a 401 or 403, so a
token mismatch shows up as an auth error instead of an empty scrape.

Evidence from running `ray metrics launch-prometheus` against a two-node
cluster with token auth on and the endpoints already requiring the
token:

- Without the `authorization` block (a manual run with the earlier
launcher), the four Ray targets (two nodes, autoscaler, dashboard) never
all come up in Prometheus's `/api/v1/targets`.
- With the block (`test_launch_prometheus_scrapes_token_auth_cluster`,
with the token from a file and from `RAY_AUTH_TOKEN`), all four targets
report `health: up`.

## Related issues

Closes #67119

## Additional information

This changes behavior for clusters that already run with token auth on,
including local clusters, which have had it on by default since 2.59.
Any Prometheus that scrapes their metrics endpoints without the token
starts getting 401s once this merges, and has to add the `authorization`
block above. Clusters with `RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled` see no change.
Reverting the PR restores open endpoints, with no data or state to
migrate.

---------

commit.message:
[Core/Auth] Add RAY_AUTH_SKIP_METRICS to serve Ray's metrics endpoints without the auth token (#67264)

## Description

With token auth on, Ray's metrics endpoints require the token since
#67128, and the only way to scrape them without one was to turn auth off
for the whole cluster. Some scrapers can't send a bearer token, and some
users protect the metrics port at the network layer instead. Setting
`RAY_AUTH_SKIP_METRICS=1` on every node now serves Ray's metrics
endpoints (each node's metrics port, the dashboard head and both
autoscaler monitors) without the token, while `RAY_AUTH_MODE=token`
still protects everything else.

```text
metrics request (get_token_auth_wsgi_app)
  auth off                       -> serve metrics (unchanged)
  RAY_AUTH_SKIP_METRICS=1        -> serve metrics without a token
  otherwise                      -> token check from #67128 (401 / 403 / serve)
```

All three metrics servers already go through `get_token_auth_wsgi_app`,
so the skip is checked there once. The env var is read with `env_bool`,
so `true` works as well as `1`. Each Ray process reads it from its own
environment, so it must be set wherever a node starts, for example in
`ray up` start commands or KubeRay pod specs.

When the skip is also set in the shell that runs `ray metrics
launch-prometheus`, it writes no `authorization` block and runs
Prometheus with the bundled config unchanged. Its warning for when it
finds no token now says that every Ray target returns 401 unless the
cluster's nodes set `RAY_AUTH_SKIP_METRICS=1`, since the launcher can't
see the nodes' setting. With auth off, the env var changes nothing.

## Related issues

Closes #67251

## Additional information

The opt-out is off unless the env var is set, so clusters that don't set
it behave exactly as after #67128.

---------

commit.message:
[Docs][Core/Auth] Document CloudWatch Prometheus scraping with token auth on (#67313)

## Description

With token auth on, Ray's metrics endpoints return 401 to a scrape
without the token (#67119). The `prometheus.yml` that the AWS CloudWatch
integration copies to the CloudWatch agent has no `authorization` block,
so no Ray metrics reach CloudWatch. Step 5 of "Monitor Ray using Amazon
CloudWatch" in `aws.md` now adds a `head_setup_commands` line that
appends the token to the `ray` scrape job of the copied config:

```diff
 - job_name: 'ray'
   file_sd_configs:
   - files:
     - '/tmp/ray/prom_metrics_service_discovery.json'
     refresh_interval: 1m
+  authorization:
+    type: Bearer
+    credentials_file: /home/ubuntu/.ray/auth_token
```

`credentials_file` must be an absolute path. The CloudWatch agent runs
as root, so `~/.ray/auth_token` doesn't reach the token in the home
directory of the user that runs Ray. The shipped `prometheus.yml` and
`example-cloudwatch.yaml` don't change.

Verified on AWS in us-west-2 with a head and one worker on the `aws.md`
DLAMI for us-west-2 (`ami-0cfd95c6c87d00570`, CloudWatch agent
1.300057.1b1167). The AMI in `example-cloudwatch.yaml`,
`ami-0d88d9cbe28fac870`, was not used because `aws ec2 describe-images`
no longer returns it. Ray came from a wheel built at 8f8e42666b, with
`RAY_AUTH_MODE=token` and the token at `/home/ubuntu/.ray/auth_token` on
every node. Each of the 4 Ray targets returned 401 to `curl` without the
token and 200 with it. The table counts CloudWatch EMF log events in
`<cluster>-ray-prometheus` after each config change, over 2 minutes (90
seconds for the `~` path):

| `ray` scrape job | Events |
|---|---|
| Shipped, no `authorization` | 0 |
| `credentials_file: ~/.ray/auth_token` | 0 |
| `credentials_file: /home/ubuntu/.ray/auth_token` | 2282, from all 4
targets |

## Related issues

Closes #67214

## Additional information

The Docker mode of `ray up` isn't covered. The token file's path on the
host wasn't checked there, and `example-cloudwatch.yaml` has no Docker
section.

The AWS run needed two steps unrelated to token auth: `sudo touch
/usr/share/collectd/types.db` on each node, because the DLAMI lacks the
file and the example agent config enables collectd, and dropping the
example alarm config, whose `AlarmActions` is a placeholder ARN.

Signed-off-by: Chi-Sheng Liu <chishengliu@chishengliu.com>

commit.message:
[fix][autoscaler] recover from WrongClusterID on head restart (#60860)

## Description

Previously, when the head node restarts, GCS gets a new cluster ID
causing the autoscaler's existing GCS client to fail with
AuthenticationError.

This fix addresses this by raising the error to exit the autoscaler main
process and let Kubernetes restart a new autoscaler container to fix the
issue.

Note that this issue arises
when`spec.headGroupSpec.template.spec.restartPolicy` is unset, which
defaults to Always, without `spec.autoscalerOptions.version: v2`.
  
Other configurations are unaffected:
- `spec.autoscalerOptions.version: v2`: 
KubeRay operator forces restartPolicy: Never and recreates the entire
pod on head failure, so the autoscaler sidecar is always fresh
- `spec.autoscalerOptions.version: v2` with `restartPolicy: Always`: 
Rejected by the KubeRay operator

## Related issues

Fixes #60534 

## Additional information

### Testing plan
   - [x] Unit tests
   - [x] Manual test with kuberay
   
   Manul Testing Steps

1. Build local images, noted this built is based on nightly version
which is **post 2.46.0**
```bash
docker build --progress=plain \
    --build-arg BUILD_DATE="$(date +%Y-%m-%d:%H:%M:%S)" \
    -t rayproject/autoscaling_e2e_test_image \
    -f ./python/ray/tests/kuberay/Dockerfile .
```

2. loaded into kind cluster
```
kind create cluster --name test-cluster-autoscaler --image kindest/node:v1.35.0
kind load docker-image rayproject/autoscaling_e2e_test_image:latest --name test-cluster-autoscaler
```

3. Install kuberay-operator
```
helm repo update
helm install kuberay-operator kuberay/kuberay-operator --version 1.5.1
```

            name: gcs
          - containerPort: 8265
            name: dashboard
          - containerPort: 10001

    ray.kill(detached_actor)

commit.message:

commit.message:
[core][sandbox] Default network="public" egress to the public internet and enforce allowlists (#66359)

## Description

A `network="public"` sandbox could reach everything its pod reaches.
From a sandbox in a CoreWeave pod running a Ray head, GCS, the Ray
client server, the raylet, the object manager, the dashboard agent, the
Kubernetes API, the kubelet, and 169.254.169.254 all accepted
connections. Ray's ports take no token unless the cluster runs with
`RAY_AUTH_MODE=token`, and slirp4netns relays sandbox flows through the
pod's own sockets, so a pod NetworkPolicy can't single them out.

This PR filters every `public` sandbox's egress with an nftables ruleset
in its private network namespace, loaded after slirp4netns brings the
tap up and before runsc starts. A failed load fails the create.

- `cidr_allowlist` defaults to `["internet"]`, public addresses only.
Entries are addresses or networks with optional ports (`10.0.0.5:8000`,
`internet:443`).
- A denylist runs before any list: link-local (instance metadata),
loopback, Alibaba Cloud's and Azure's metadata endpoints, the Kubernetes
API Service, and `RAY_SANDBOX_EGRESS_DENY`. Ray doesn't track its nodes,
as pcmoritz suggested: `internet` leaves them out while their addresses
are internal, which the docs call a best effort, and an operator who
allows internal networks lists the nodes' network in
`RAY_SANDBOX_EGRESS_DENY`, which also covers nodes the autoscaler adds.
- `set_egress_allowlist`, on `SandboxRuntime` and on the actor that
`sandbox.create()` returns, replaces any public sandbox's ruleset in one
`nft -f`, entering its namespaces through fds checked against the ones
recorded at creation.
- With `dns` set, the create sends each resolver one UDP byte from
inside the sandbox and fails, naming the resolver, if the send fails. On
Cilium, which translates the cluster DNS Service IP before the filter
sees it, every lookup failed instead.
- The gRPC facade maps `block_network`, `outbound_cidr_allowlist`, and
`TaskSetNetworkAccess`; open access means `internet`.
- The REST API answers 403 to `network="host"`, `"sandbox"`, or
`rootless=false` unless `allowed_network_modes` / `allow_rootful` allow
them, and `build_app` requires `RAY_SANDBOX_API_TOKEN` unless
`allow_unauthenticated` is set.

Behavior changes: `public` needs `nft` on the node, no longer reaches
private networks without a list, and fails to create when a `dns`
resolver is unreachable. REST deployments need a token.

### Why nftables inside the sandbox netns is the right enforcement point

Inside the sandbox's private user + net namespace, the host-side launch
script has CAP_NET_ADMIN over that child network namespace (without
needing CAP_NET_ADMIN on the Kubernetes worker pod itself).

runsc runs inside that child netns with --network=host. That means
gVisor's hostinet creates real Linux kernel AF_INET/AF_INET6 sockets
inside the child netns, so every packet from the sandbox passes through
the Linux kernel's nf_tables output chain before reaching slirp4netns's
tap0.

**Why sandbox code cannot tamper with the rules (even with
CAP_NET_ADMIN):** gVisor's Sentry intercepts all syscalls inside the
sandbox. Even if the container process has CAP_NET_ADMIN or CAP_NET_RAW,
gVisor's hostinet (without --net-raw) never forwards AF_NETLINK
(NETLINK_NETFILTER / NETLINK_ROUTE) or AF_PACKET sockets to the host
kernel. Running nft flush ruleset or iptables -F inside the sandbox
talks only to gVisor's internal Sentry stub, never touching the host
kernel netns where the rules live.

### Results

TCP connects from a sandbox in a CoreWeave (Cilium) pod running a Ray
head, 5 s timeout, measured on dddd170d9b9:

| Destination | Default | `ALLOW_ALL_CIDRS` | +
`RAY_SANDBOX_EGRESS_DENY=<node>,<API server>` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GCS, Ray client server, raylet, object manager, dashboard | timeout |
open | timeout |
| 169.254.169.254:80 | timeout | timeout | timeout |
| Kubernetes API (Service and endpoint) | timeout | open | timeout |
| 1.1.1.1:443, DNS | open | open | open |

Allow-all reaches the Ray head's ports because Ray doesn't track its
nodes, and it reaches the API Service because Cilium rewrites it to the
API server's address at connect time; `RAY_SANDBOX_EGRESS_DENY` closes
both, and the docs say so. Root in a sandbox with `CAP_NET_ADMIN` and
`CAP_NET_RAW` ran `nft flush ruleset` and `iptables -F`: both failed
with "Protocol not supported", and GCS stayed closed.

How to review: `config.py`, `_internal/egress_guard.py`,
`backend/gvisor.py` (`_render_egress_ruleset`, the run command,
`set_egress_allowlist`, `_unreachable_resolver`), `http/host.py` and
`http/grpc_facade.py`, `http/schemas.py` and `http/app.py`, then the
docs. Skip the `_pb2.py` files.

## Related issues

Follows #65839. Found through SkyRL's SWE-bench Multimodal runs on Ray
Sandbox (NovaSky-AI/SkyRL#2467). #66782 and #67010 inherit the default.
#66471's restore path needs the same nft install.

## Additional information

- Not a duplicate: none of the 20 open sandbox PRs adds egress filtering
or a default deny.
- Tests on a CoreWeave pod (Cilium, runsc release-20261012.0, root),
rebased on master 7073066e85d: `TEST_SANDBOX=1 pytest
tests/test_gvisor_backend.py tests/test_image_manager.py
tests/test_image_utils.py tests/test_sandbox_config.py
tests/test_sandbox_runtime.py tests/test_egress_guard.py -k "not netns
and not test_create_sandbox_helper"`: 167 passed, 1 skipped. `-k netns`:
22 passed. `test_create_sandbox_helper`: 1 passed.
`tests/test_sandbox.py`: 7 passed. `http/tests`: 167 passed, 10 skipped.
With the Modal SDK 1.5.5 installed on macOS, which CI doesn't have,
`http/tests`: 175 passed, 2 skipped (the gVisor integration tests). On
the pod, `dns=["10.16.0.10"]`, the cluster DNS Service, now fails the
create with "Operation not permitted" and still resolves with
`ALLOW_ALL_CIDRS`; the check adds about 14 ms to a create. pre-commit
passes. This round wasn't rerun as uid 1000.
- I used Claude Code to help write and test this change.

---------

Co-authored-by: Philipp Moritz <pcmoritz@gmail.com>
